config.title: Tempelhofer Feld - FAQ
config.subtitle: When Tempelhofer Feld opens and closes, which of its ten gates to use for what you came for, and how to get out once the gates are locked.

items.q: What time does Tempelhofer Feld close?
items.a: **It depends on the month, and the swing is large.** Grün Berlin sets the hours by season: January and December **07:30 to 17:00**, February **07:00 to 18:00**, March **06:00 to 19:00**, April **06:00 to 20:30**, 1 to 15 May **06:00 to 21:30**, 16 to 31 May **06:00 to 22:00**, June and July **06:00 to 23:00**, August **06:00 to 22:30**, September **06:30 to 21:30**, October **07:00 to 19:00**, November **07:00 to 18:00**. The step from August to October removes three and a half hours of evening, and the change happens on the first of the month, so check before an evening visit.

items.q: Can you get out of Tempelhofer Feld after it closes?
items.a: **Yes, through five gates.** Tempelhofer Damm, Columbiadamm, Oderstraße/Herrfurthstraße, Oderstraße/Crash Gate and Leinestraße each keep a full-height turnstile that works at any hour. It lets you out and never in. The other five gates are locked. A turnstile turns one person at a time, so with a bike, a pram or a picnic to carry it is slow. Be at a gate about fifteen minutes before closing instead of at it. Note that the operator's FAQ page lists only four of those exits and leaves Leinestraße out, while its visitor page lists all five.

items.q: Which entrance to Tempelhofer Feld should I use?
items.a: **Pick it by what you came for, because the field is 2,246 metres across.** For a barbecue use **Columbiadamm**: the three permitted grill areas are 175 metres inside that gate and 1,737 metres from the Tempelhofer Damm gate. For the community gardens and the Schillerkiez cafés use the **Oderstraße** gates, where the gardens are 75 to 230 metres inside the fence. For the runways and the open sky almost any gate works, though the eastern gates put you on concrete within about a hundred metres. For the quickest arrival from central Berlin use **Tempelhofer Damm**, 113 metres from S+U Tempelhof.

items.q: How do you get to Tempelhofer Feld by public transport?
items.a: **S+U Tempelhof is the fastest**, 113 metres from the main west gate, with U6 and Ringbahn services S41, S42, S46 and S47. **Bus M43** stops at Friedhöfe Columbiadamm, 46 metres from the northern main gate, and also runs from U Boddinstraße. **U8** to Boddinstraße or Leinestraße puts you a six to seven minute walk from the Oderstraße gates on the east side. **U6** to Paradestraße is about 226 metres from the Tor 10 gate. There is almost no parking, so the operator asks visitors to come by public transport.

items.q: Can you barbecue on Tempelhofer Feld?
items.a: **Only in the three marked barbecue areas**, all of which are at the Columbiadamm end of the field. The grill must stand on **legs at least 25 cm high** so it does not damage the turf, and **footless disposable trays and gas grills are not allowed**. Hot ash and charcoal must not go into the plastic waste containers because of the fire risk. If you arrive at any other gate carrying charcoal, expect a walk of up to 1,700 metres to reach a legal grill.

items.q: Why is part of Tempelhofer Feld fenced off?
items.a: **Skylarks nest in the grass.** From roughly late March or early April until the end of August the inner meadows between the two runways are closed and posted with signs, because the skylark is a ground-nesting bird and the field is one of its last real breeding sites inside Berlin. A line of bollards runs fifteen metres back from each runway with information boards along it, and the eastern half of the ground south of the southern runway is fenced against entry all year. Park supervision enforces it. Dogs must be on the lead, which matters most in those months.

**Yes, if you go for the space rather than for attractions.** It is two kilometres of Cold War runway you can walk, cycle or skate, with beer gardens at the north end, community gardens at the east, and a twenty-station history trail covering the Berlin Airlift, the wartime forced-labour camp and the Columbia-Haus, the only official SS concentration camp inside the city of Berlin between 1934 and 1936. Berliners voted in a 2014 referendum against building on it and the result became law, which is why the horizon is still unbroken. Entry is free.
